opex.name: Compensation and benefits
opex.note: Pay for the people who run the markets and build the software — the biggest running cost, up 7% as headcount grew.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Mostly spreading the purchase price of past acquisitions (like the Adenza deal) over time — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: Technology & facilities
opex.note: The systems and communications that keep trading running ($93M) plus offices and occupancy ($34M).

opex.name: Professional, marketing & other
opex.note: Outside professional and contract services ($42M), marketing ($17M), regulatory fees ($11M), merger and strategy work ($6M) and general & administrative costs ($2M).

footerNote: Nasdaq passes a large share of trading revenue straight back out as transaction rebates ($623M) and brokerage, clearance and exchange fees ($289M) — those are treated here as the cost of revenue, matching Nasdaq's own 'revenues less transaction-based expenses' line of $1,481M. Operating-expense lines are grouped from the release's ten lines into four; the total ($749M) is unchanged.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $86M, partly offset by $38M earned from unconsolidated investees, $11M of other income and $10M of interest income, plus a $4M loss on divestitures — a net $31M cost below operating profit.

segments.name: Capital Access Platforms
segments.note: Listing fees, the index business and corporate data services. Index revenue alone grew 39% to $286M, with $49B of net inflows into Nasdaq-indexed products in the quarter. Segment revenue up 20%.

segments.name: Financial Technology
segments.note: Software sold to banks, brokers and exchanges — anti-financial-crime tools, regulatory reporting and market technology. Recurring by nature; revenue up 16%.

segments.name: Market Services
segments.note: The trading venues themselves — stocks, options, futures and digital-asset market infrastructure. Gross revenue up 26% on heavy trading volumes; much of it is paid back out as rebates and fees (see cost of revenue).

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: A small residual line, down from $21M a year ago.

takeaways.text: Market Services gross revenue jumped to $1,221M on surging trading volumes. After paying out $912M of rebates and pass-through fees, Nasdaq kept $1,481M of net revenue — up 13% — and a record quarter for its new Digital Liquidity Networks business.
takeaways.title: Trading volumes surged

takeaways.text: Index revenue grew 39% to $286M as investors poured $49B into Nasdaq-indexed products in the quarter ($141B over twelve months) — high-margin money that arrives whether or not trading is busy.
takeaways.title: The index business is booming

takeaways.text: Annualized recurring revenue reached $3.4B, up 12%, and Solutions revenue grew 17%. The steady software-and-data income is why profit rose 27% even in a business built on volatile trading.
takeaways.title: Recurring revenue keeps compounding

verdict: Profit rose 27% to $539M as trading volumes surged and the index and software businesses kept compounding — net revenue grew 13% to $1.5B.
